question.worked_solution:
We start by writing the root as a rational power, $\sqrt{{x}^{3}}={x}^{3/2}.$ So, we can apply the power rule with $n=\frac{3}{2}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \sqrt{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\int {x}^{3/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3/2+1}}{(\frac{3}{2}+1)}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{5/2}}{(\frac{5}{2})}+C \\  & =\frac{2{x}^{5/2}}{5}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, let's check by differentiating:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{2{x}^{5/2}}{5}+C) & = \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{2{x}^{5/2}}{5})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) & = \\ \frac{2}{5}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{5/2})+0 & = \\ \frac{2}{5}\cdot \frac{5}{2}{x}^{5/2-1} & = \\ {x}^{3/2}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
